title: sys_business_unit_member: the record title shows raw ids (user id in business unit id) instead of the person's and the unit's names
body:
Filing gate ②: a maintainer ruling, carried out as child 9 of the nine that #26059's ruling (Q3) names. ⛔ Not a claim.

The Title column in Setup → Business Unit Members, and the record page heading, read "<userId> in <businessUnitId>": two opaque ids, with no person or department name. This is not a rendering bug. The object's title is declared as a formula over the two stored lookup ids, so the title is the ids by definition. It needs to be built from the two lookups' display names instead.

Part of #26059
Ruling-ref: 6416233738 (https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/26059#issuecomment-6416233738)
Ruling: batch #396 item 1, letter Q1 是 / Q2 不做 / Q3 分拆 / Q4 框架. This card is Q3 child 9 (server, p3): item 8. Brief 6415795834, item-by-item reading 6415971852 (item 8).
Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`domain:ui#2`) · `os-steve` · session `session_01SMps7wq7rBTk53e8KTSEup`, first claimant of #26059. Domain, grade and route are triage's on first touch.

**Business reason.** An admin checking who belongs to which department reads a column of ids and has to open each row to find out. Any other surface that names a membership record by its title shows the same ids.

**Reader who acts.** The `domain:server` execution seat, dispatch step: one os-dev, one PR in `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/`. The PR touches the formula runtime or a hook only if the mechanism chosen below needs it.

**Spec contract.** None is expected to change. If the chosen mechanism needs a formula capability that does not exist, say so on this card before building. Do not widen `@objectstack/formula` silently.

**Duplicate check.** A local scan of the 1,962 newest issues (all states, #22168–#26181) for `sys_business_unit_member.{0,200}(title|display)|display_title.{0,100}business_unit` found 0 hits.

## Ruled scope (ruling Q3 item 9)

- `sys_business_unit_member`'s title is built **over the two lookups' display names** instead of `record.user_id + ' in ' + record.business_unit_id` (`sys-business-unit-member.object.ts:38, :52–55`).
- **The dev names the mechanism first.** Either a formula over related display names, or a stamped title kept up to date by a hook on both ids. The reading did not find a lookup-display helper in `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`.

## Anchors (re-read on `origin/main` `83a26c38`)

- `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-business-unit-member.object.ts`:
  - `:38` `titleFormat: '{user_id} in {business_unit_id}'` holds.
  - `:52–58` is the `display_title` formula field; the expression ``F`record.user_id + ' in ' + record.business_unit_id` `` is at `:55`. The ruling's `:52–55` holds.
  - The file's own comment at `:33–35` already states the limit: "a formula is evaluated on the stored row, before `$expand`, and cannot reach a related record's own title". That confirms the mechanism has to be named before any code.
- `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/identity-display-title.test.ts` holds `titleFormat` and `display_title` to the same text, so both move together.
- `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`: no lookup-display helper found (re-checked).

## Expected / acceptance

- The mechanism is named on this card before code, with its cost on writes and reads.
- The list Title column and the record heading show "<user's name> in <business unit's name>".
- The title follows a change of either `user_id` or `business_unit_id`. A renamed user or unit shows the new name; if the mechanism is a stamp, the PR says how far that goes.
- `titleFormat` and `display_title` still agree (`identity-display-title.test.ts`). A test covers the named title.
